sources.title: Archon: Quickstart; Connect a platform
sources.finding: Archon has a product CLI and self-hosted browser console. macOS/Linux and Windows installers are documented, and Slack/Telegram/GitHub adapters are separate conversation channels. Installable CLI platforms do not establish native desktop GUIs.

sources.title: Archon: Your agents, your subscriptions; Plugin kinds
sources.locator: Your agents, your subscriptions; Plugin kinds
sources.finding: Maintained provider plugins run Claude Code, Codex and Pi using their CLIs/SDKs. Community providers use a published contract; compatibility and workflow capabilities are provider-specific.

sources.title: Archon: Your agents, your subscriptions; Quickstart
sources.finding: Archon runs existing Claude Code, Codex and Pi accounts. The quickstart asks users to install and sign into Claude Code or Codex before setup.

sources.title: Archon: Quickstart
sources.finding: Users install and sign in to Claude Code or install Codex, install Archon, then run a named workflow in any git repository.

sources.title: Archon: API Reference; Authentication
sources.finding: Archon exposes a REST API under /api with OpenAPI 3 generation. Solo local authentication is optional; configured web auth requires a session or trusted proxy identity. The CLI controls workflow runs and approvals.

sources.title: Archon: A reliable core; Plugin kinds
sources.finding: Versioned plugins supply workflow packs, agent providers, forges and chat adapters through a published contract and install from GitHub; users can build their own plugins.

sources.title: Archon: A software factory
sources.finding: The SDLC pack takes GitHub issues through intake, build and merge queues via the forge plugin. External issues remain the durable intake objects; this is not the archived native RAG/task app.

sources.title: Archon: Workflow language
sources.finding: YAML workflows declare ordered or dependent agent, script, loop, wait and approval nodes, with output contracts and persisted runs. Workflow files can be edited and versioned in the project.

sources.title: Archon: Separate governed child runs; fan_out
sources.finding: A workflow node can launch separate child runs with their own identity, artifacts, costs and pauses. Dependencies and fan-out govern execution; max_parallel caps concurrent children rather than total work.

sources.title: Archon: Your agents; Workflow packs
sources.finding: Archon reuses provider project guidance and stores workflow commands and scripts beside YAML. This does not establish a shared cross-provider semantic memory store.

sources.title: Archon: A software factory
sources.finding: The discoveries workflow reads out-of-task findings and files them as new GitHub issues or attaches them to existing issues through the forge plugin. Native issue object parity is not asserted.

sources.title: Archon: fan_out; Concurrency
sources.finding: Workflow fan-out creates concurrent governed child runs and max_parallel limits active children. Parent and child records remain inspectable.

sources.title: Archon: A software factory
sources.finding: The build queue claims ready issues; the merge queue processes ready PRs and returns conflicts for rework. The bundled pack binds no triggers by default.

sources.title: Archon: Launching a separate governed run
sources.finding: The product assistant can invoke workflows and inspect runs; workflow nodes delegate child runs with output returned to their parent, separate artifacts, pauses and cost records.

sources.title: Archon: Start workflows from schedules and signed webhooks
sources.locator: Start workflows from schedules and signed webhooks
sources.finding: Native schedules, GitHub events and Standard Webhooks request governed runs with host identity, overlap policy and resource admission. The configured server or detached CLI host starts admitted work and deduplicates shared admission records.

sources.title: Archon: Workflows and runs; Alerts
sources.finding: Console actions include approve, reject, resume, cancel and abandon. Optional alerts announce approval/attention waits, completion, failure and cancellation.

sources.title: Archon: Console navigation; Workflows and runs
sources.finding: The console lists runs across projects and exposes per-run event logs, artifacts and graph context when the workflow definition is available. Fleet-navigation effort was not measured.

sources.title: Archon: Build any factory; Quickstart
sources.finding: Users invoke a ready workflow in natural language or edit the YAML graph to combine agent prompts, scripts, waits, loops and child workflows.

sources.title: Archon: Deployment overview
sources.finding: Archon can run locally for development or be deployed with Docker or on a cloud VPS for always-on operation, using SQLite by default or PostgreSQL.

sources.title: Archon: What it looks like
sources.finding: Repository runs receive their own Git worktree by default, permitting separate runs against the same repository.

sources.title: Archon: How it works; Provider support; Security posture
sources.locator: How it works; Provider support; Security posture
sources.finding: Folder projects optionally run in Docker with read-only project root, overlay writes and approval-gated write-back. Only Claude nodes currently support this container mode; other providers fail before execution. Native overlay fallback uses CAP_SYS_ADMIN and is not hostile-agent containment.

sources.title: Archon: Pause economics
sources.finding: Normal container pauses stop compute; resume can restart or recreate the container from its persisted upper volume. Missing volumes fail loudly. Web/chat decisions cannot continue container execution; a same-project CLI resume is required.

sources.title: Archon: Prerequisites; Running
sources.finding: Container runs require Docker and a current runner image containing tools. Artifacts are retained through a dedicated writable bind; stopped containers preserve their upper volume for resume.

sources.title: Archon: Run budgets; Retry policy
sources.finding: Optional run budgets enforce work-unit and provider-reported USD spend ceilings before new attempts. In-flight work can overshoot spend, unknown cost fails a spend-capped run, and budgeted nested/loop shapes are rejected if unsupported.

sources.title: Archon: Workflows and runs
sources.finding: Run details expose event logs and artifacts; live events show governance state. Documentation describes retry and failure records but no induced worker-failure consistency test was run.

sources.title: Archon: Cost roll-up; Reading tokens and cost
sources.locator: Cost roll-up; Reading tokens and cost
sources.finding: Child run costs roll up into parents without duplicating prior resumed increments; per-run token and provider-cost records persist even for failed fan-out. Unknown provider cost stays unknown.

sources.title: Archon: Governed admission
sources.finding: Trigger bindings declare host, shared resource and overlap policy and share admission records. Workflow fan-out adds max_parallel limits. This is not a measured host-load safety test.

sources.title: Archon: Users and roles; Who can act on a run
sources.locator: Users and roles; Who can act on a run
sources.finding: New identities are members. Operators designate admins; only a run starter or an admin can perform governance actions on that run. Solo installs may leave web auth disabled.

sources.title: Archon: Approval nodes
sources.finding: Workflow approval gates pause for explicit approve or reject decisions, can rework on rejection and record decisions in the run. Broader shell policy remains provider-specific.

sources.title: Archon: Governance built in
sources.finding: Each run retains an event log, transcript and cost in the user database. The docs call this an audit trail; immutable retention and tamper resistance were not independently established.
